members.title: Tennessee governor halts executions after second botched lethal injection attempt this year – US politics live
members.lead: Bill Lee pauses state’s remaining executions for the rest of the year after inmate Christa Pike survives two lethal injections Tennessee woman on death row taken to hospital after surviving two lethal injections Sign up for the Breaking News US email On that note, Donald Trump will begin his day in Washington in closed-door meetings. He’ll then start his day of campaigning to Republican strongholds. First up, the president will be in Denton, Texas, where he’ll tour the Peterbilt truck manufacturing facility at 4pm ET. Then heads to Durant, Oklahoma – which sits just north of the Texas border – to give a speech at 7pm ET. President Donald Trump and vice-president JD Vance will both hit the campaign trail on Thursday, but they will be heading to heavily Republican areas to shore up lagging enthusiasm in their party ahead of next month’s midterm elections. members.title: Tennessee governor suspends all executions after Christa Pike’s lethal injections fail
members.lead: Independent inquiry ordered after failed execution of Pike, who was convicted of 1994 murder Christa Pike: what we know so far about Tennessee woman’s failed execution Tennessee’s governor on Thursday said it was “deeply disturbing” that his state botched the execution of a death row prisoner who remained alive and snoring 40 minutes after receiving a double dose of the lethal drug that should have quickly killed her. Bill Lee, a Republican, has suspended all executions in the state until at least the end of the year and ordered an independent inquiry after Wednesday night’s failed attempt to put to death Christa Pike, who was convicted of murder, at the execution chamber in Nashville. members.title: Witnesses detail horror of Tennessee woman’s botched execution: ‘None of it was normal’
members.lead: Witnesses in the chamber said Christa Pike was still breathing despite receiving injections intended to kill her When the prison warden asked Christa Pike if she had any last words, she said she was going to leave this world “with love” for those on her side and also the ones angry with her. What followed was the second botched execution in Tennessee this year, after two doses of the lethal injection failed to produce the desired effect. Continue reading...
